subject: Activation checklist & control-plane ownership for Private VPC deployment (Orion Health)
messages:
From: Sara Patel <sara.patel@orionhealth.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-12-15T09:23:00-08:00
Subject: Private VPC activation – initial inventory and ownership

Hi Jordan,

Thanks for taking this on. We're aiming to start the private deployment activation window the week of Jan 11. Before we lock dates, security and infra need a short list of the items you require from us so the activation run isn't blocked. Specifically: 

- Control plane ownership and contact (who at Redwood will own control-plane configuration and post-cutover support)
- Required firewall/egress ports and recommended IP ranges (we'll need both a staging and prod allowlist)
- Service accounts and KMS/HSM integration guidance (we plan to use our existing KMS)
- Any required inventory template for hosts, subnets, and BGP/VPN details

I've attached a quick network scan and our current inventory export for reference. Please share a concise checklist we can assign to our cloud networking and security teams.

Best,
Sara
Sara Patel
Engineering Manager, Cloud Operations
Orion Health

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-12-15T11:10:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Private VPC activation – initial inventory and ownership

Sara — thanks for the quick context and the scan. We're aligned to keep the Jan 11 window as tentative; we'll firm once the artifacts below are in place. High-level answers and an action checklist attached (redwood-predeploy-checklist-v1.pdf). Key points inline: 

1) Control plane ownership:
- Primary: Jordan Blake (ONCALL: infra-redwood) — control-plane configs, rollout coordination, escalation to runtime team.
- Secondary (post-cutover): Marissa Cole — operations & billing handoff.

2) Firewall / egress allowlist:
- Recommended ports: 443 (TLS), 22 (SSH) only for provisioning windows, and 32400-32416 (custom management port range) for agent-heartbeat and metrics (if you opt into hosted telemetry).
- IP ranges: we will provide a /29 per environment (staging/prod) in a follow-up CIDR envelope.

3) Service accounts and KMS:
- We can support customer-managed KMS. Please provide the KMS key ARN and a service account with kms:Decrypt and kms:GenerateDataKey permissions. We will hand over a minimal trust policy.

4) Inventory template:
- Attached: env_inventory.csv template and a sample network-diagram-v3.png. Please populate subnets, gateway IPs, NAT requirements, and VPN endpoints (if using VPN).

Next steps:
- If you can return the completed env_inventory.csv and confirm the KMS key by EOD 2026-12-18, we'll lock the Jan 11 activation window and schedule a 60-minute preflight call.

Attachments: redwood-predeploy-checklist-v1.pdf, env_inventory.csv, network-diagram-v3.png

—Jordan
Jordan Blake

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-12-16T08:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Private VPC activation – initial inventory and ownership

Quick technical notes from runtime team:

- Network MTU: target 9000 where possible for GPU-backed inference clusters; if your network doesn't support jumbo frames, we can tune batch sizes but expect ~10-15% throughput impact.
- KV cache traffic: peer-to-peer TCP on the management ports; ensure low-latency links between inference hosts and the control plane (preferably sub-1ms within same AZ/rack).
- Persistent storage: Redwood agents require an NFS mount option for logs/metrics or an S3-compatible endpoint; if you expose S3 within VPC, provide the endpoint URL and role.
- BGP/VPN: we support both. If you use BGP, share ASNs and route filters. For IPSec VPNs, we need IKE proposals and pre-shared keys during the preflight call (do not send keys via email).

I'll join the preflight call to review the inventory and confirm kernel/quantization profiles if any of your models are quantized.

-Karthik
Principal Infrastructure Engineer

Thanks all — let's keep this light-touch.
